vol_fft_highpass — 3D frequency op

• Data kinds: voxel → voxel

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.vol_fft_highpass(vol, cutoff, spacing=None) (to call the implementation directly, import volfreq; volfreq.vol_fft_highpass(vol, cutoff, spacing=None); from the registry, ops3d.get("vol_fft_highpass"))

Usage

Gaussian high-pass — the exact complement 1 - lowpass (the two sum to the input).

The sum holds to float precision, proven in tests. Removes the DC level and slow drift, keeps edges/texture. Output is signed (mean ~ 0).

The transfer function is 1 - exp(-|f|^2 / (2 cutoff^2)). The DC (f = 0) coefficient is 0, so the mean luminance is removed completely; at |f| = cutoff it is 1 - 0.61 ≈ 0.39, and it approaches 1 at higher frequencies. The return value is float64 of the same (D, H, W) as the input and is signed (contains negative values). To pass it to later stages that assume [0, 1] (display, vol_window_level etc.), normalise it with vol_stretch or use it in the form vol + highpass.

Arguments: cutoff is a positive finite value. With spacing=None it is cycles/voxel; passing spacing ((sz, sy, sx) or volio.VolumeMeta) makes it cycles/mm.

Validation (ValueError): same as vol_fft_lowpass (not 3-D / NaN or Inf / over MAX_VOXELS / invalid cutoff or spacing).

Where to use it: removing uneven illumination, thickness drift and background gradients (equivalent to subtracting the result of vol_fft_lowpass). Because the FFT treats the volume as periodic, luminance differences between faces leak through the wrap.
